question.text: The mass of sodium acetate <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>CH</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mi>COONa</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> required to prepare <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>250</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>35</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></math> aqueous solution is _____ g.<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close=""><mrow></mrow></mfenced></math> Molar mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CH</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mi>COONa</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>82</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>02</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>) Round off to the nearest integer.

solution.text:
Given, Molarity= 0.35 M

Moles = Molarity × Volume in litres

=0.35×0.25

No. of moles = Mass/ Molar mass 

Mass = moles ×molar mass

=0.35×0.25×82.02=7.18 g

Ans. 7
